analysis: Simple test battery on 2^20 outputs - PCG64 passes everything; the anchored Fibonacci generator x + y + 1 on Z/2^32 and the affine magma x + beta y + 1 fail low-byte uniformity (p = 0; Fibonacci-type sequences are not uniformly distributed modulo 2^k) and their lowest bit has period 3; the LCG fails the low-bit tests (period 2, low byte too regular); the de Bruijn byte magma, whose period 65536 is the maximum possible for an order-2 byte recurrence, is too regular in every frequency test. No magma generator is competitive.
assumptions: tests: chi-square of the top byte and of the low byte, serial chi-square of consecutive top-byte pairs, lowest-bit period (searched up to 2^16), lag-1 correlation; p-values from scipy.stats
this is a sanity battery, not TestU01/PractRand
falsification: A magma generator passing every test at the 1% level with a period comparable to the baselines.

hypothesis: H-C16-10 (Application Researcher): none of the magma generators passes the simple test battery as well as PCG64; the anchored Fibonacci generator fails low-bit tests (Fibonacci numbers are not uniformly distributed modulo 2^k) and the de Bruijn byte generator is too regular.
methodology: Generators: G1 anchored associative magma on Z/2^32, x_{k+1} = x_k + x_{k-1} + 1; G2 affine magma x_{k+1} = x_k + beta x_{k-1} + 1 (beta = 0x9E3779B9); G3 the de Bruijn byte magma (full period 65536 = the maximum for an order-2 byte recurrence; FKM construction); baselines PCG64 and the LCG 1664525 x + 1013904223 mod 2^32.
question: The longest pair-map periods found are n^2 (de Bruijn tables) and, for affine magmas on Z/2^32, the order of a matrix. Do such generators give usable pseudo-random numbers compared with standard generators?
